exercise1.prompt: Turning a column per month into a column that says which month.

hiddenCases.name: one person and two months gives two rows
the month names land in a column
melt does the reshaping
hiddenCases.describe: melt rather than a hand-built table

exercise1.hint: id_vars=["name"] keeps the name and folds every other column down. The row count is people times months.

questions.prompt: Why can you not group a wide table by month?
choices: The month is in the column names, not in the data
questions.explain: groupby works on values. A month that only exists as a header is not a value yet, which is exactly what melt fixes.

choices: The columns that stay as they are
questions.explain: Identifiers stay; everything else is melted. Forgetting one turns an identifier into data.

questions.prompt: Three people and four months melted gives how many rows?
questions.explain: One row per person per month. A row count that is not the product is the quickest sign the melt did not do what you meant.
